To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) a time-based scheme based on a random time interval between samples is not efficient; b) a time-based sampling strategy based on a periodic sampling interval is efficient if it is synchronized with the primary network; c) the event-based scheme is efficient and robust, and can be used in a variety of situations.
(a) the secondary users should transmit with limited power and (b) the secondary users can transmit their information with a random sampling strategy that outperforms the usual time-based strategy.
event-based schemes based on energy packets outperform the usual periodic sampling schemes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of sampling-communication schemes that can be implemented by smart meters to communicate with the utility company, while minimizing the interference in the primary uplink channels.
the development of a smart-meter-aggregator link that can be used in the context of a smart grid.
the communication of secondary users in the uplink channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed sampling-communication strategy is robust against unknown primary users' activity and can achieve a low reconstruction error for the household's average power demand.

the use of directional antennas, limited transmission power and event-based sampling can be used to improve the performance of the communication between the secondary users (meters) and the aggregator.
the event-based sampling-communication scheme is the best option in terms of power consumption and reconstruction accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy packets can be used to reduce the sampling rate, and hence, the power consumption of the smart-meters.
the event-based sampling-communication scheme outperforms the time-based sampling-communication strategy.
the energy packets approach can be a good alternative for smart-meters' communication with the aggregator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the secondary users' performance is not only a function of the primary users' traffic activity, but also of the secondary users' sampling and communication strategies.

, in the context of smart grids, the secondary users' communication can be optimized to reduce the number of transmissions and the power consumption, while guaranteeing the quality of service of the primary network.
, in order to reduce the sampling rate, the smart-meters should transmit their data when their power demand is high.
